title: Strict Roos normalization of integral pullback and constant scalar restriction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On the small pro-étale sites put $C_T=(A)_T$, $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$, and $A_{n,T}=(A/\pi^n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ and $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $\operatorname{Res}_T$ be restriction along the constant-function map $C_T\to R_T$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Pullback on either coefficient system means the module inverse image with its canonical coefficient identifications [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms].

Let $P$ be any flat-term K-flat cochain complex of $R_Y$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Set $Q=\operatorname{Res}_Y P$ and form the strict towers
$$T_n=g^*(P\otimes_{R_Y}A_{n,Y}),\quad U_n=(g^*P)\otimes_{R_X}A_{n,X},\quad V_n=g_C^*(Q\otimes_{C_Y}A_{n,Y}),$$
with transitions induced by $A/\pi^{n+1}\to A/\pi^n$ and quotient augmentations from $g^*P$ or $g_C^*Q$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For a strict tower $W$ write
$$\mathsf R(W)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nW_n\to\prod_nW_n)[-1],\qquad (s w)_n=t_n(w_{n+1}),$$
using degreewise products [def-weil-derived-limit, def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Here for a cochain map $f:B\to D$, $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^q=D^q\oplus B^{q+1}$ with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Dx+f(y),-d_By)$, and the differential on a shift by $-1$ is the negative of the shifted differential. For a compatible augmentation $b:L\to W$, write $\alpha_W(b):L\to\mathsf R(W)$ for the cone lift with unshifted coordinate $(b_n)_n$ and shifted coordinate zero.

There are canonical isomorphisms of strict cochain towers $\lambda:T\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ and $\theta:\operatorname{Res}_XT\xrightarrow{\sim}V$, and a natural chain isomorphism $d:\operatorname{Res}_X(g^*P)\xrightarrow{\sim}g_C^*Q$. Here $\lambda_n$ is the tensor-pullback balancing comparison, $d$ is normalized on scalar-extension generators by the constant-function coefficient square, and $\theta_n$ is its composite with the inverse of the constant-to-completed finite tensor comparison. Equivalently, under the canonical coefficient isomorphisms both underlying sheaf complexes in the source and target of $d$ identify with $g^{-1}P$, and the underlying map of $d$ is the identity. All these maps commute strictly with quotient transitions and quotient augmentations. Moreover $g^*P$, $Q$ and $g_C^*Q$ are flat-term K-flat complexes over their respective rings.

The induced cochain isomorphisms
$$L_P:\mathsf R(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf R(U),\qquad E_P:\operatorname{Res}_X\mathsf R(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf R(V)$$
are given in both cone coordinates by the product of the stated level maps (using the canonical product comparison for restriction of scalars), and satisfy the equalities of chain maps
$$L_P\,\alpha_T=\alpha_U,\qquad E_P\,\operatorname{Res}_X(\alpha_T)=\alpha_V\,d.$$
After localization these are the canonical strict-derived-tower comparisons: the first identifies the pulled quotient augmentation with the completion unit of $g^*[P]$, and the second identifies its scalar restriction with the constant-coefficient completed-pullback unit. The constant and completed ambient categories remain distinct. No boundedness, constructibility or completeness of $[P]$ is assumed.

proof.text: Identify $R_T$ with $\varprojlim_n A_{n,T}$ by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], using its canonical finite projections. The coefficient datum makes $A$ a discrete valuation ring, hence a principal ideal domain; every ideal is finitely generated, so $A$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] on each small pro-étale site with $I=(\pi)$. Its flatness and quotient assertions give $R_T$ flat over $C_T$ and $R_T/\pi^nR_T\cong A_{n,T}$ for every $n\geq1$, compatibly with the quotient projections. These assertions concern the entire module categories and require no completeness of $[P]$.

proof.text: Write $a_C:g^{-1}C_Y\cong C_X$ and $a_R:g^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. The constant identification comes from inverse image of constant sheaves; the completed identification and exactness of module inverse image are [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. If $i_T:C_T\to R_T$ is the constant-function map, naturality of the comparison $g^{-1}p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ at the map from discrete $A$ to continuous $A$ gives $a_R\,g^{-1}i_Y=i_Xa_C$ [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. By [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], $g^*H=R_X\otimes_{g^{-1}R_Y}g^{-1}H$. Its identification with $g^{-1}H$ sends $r\otimes h$ to $a_R^{-1}(r)h$, with inverse $h\mapsto1\otimes h$. The analogous formula using $a_C$ identifies $g_C^*\operatorname{Res}_YH$ with the same abelian sheaf. The displayed coefficient-square equation makes these two $C_X$-actions identical. Define $d_H$ by the identity on that sheaf. It therefore sends each scalar-extension generator to its specified constant-coefficient generator, is invertible, and is natural in $H$. Both module inverse images therefore have the same exact underlying abelian inverse-image functor. Applying the construction in every degree gives a chain isomorphism for every complex $H$, in particular $d=d_P$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat] to $C_Y\to R_Y$, flat by step 1. Since $P$ is K-flat with flat terms, $Q=\operatorname{Res}_YP$ is K-flat with flat terms over $C_Y$. Apply the flat-term K-flat pullback assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the ringed-topos morphisms with coefficients $R_Y,R_X$ and $C_Y,C_X$, respectively. It gives flat terms and K-flatness for $g^*P$ and $g_C^*Q$. These applications impose neither boundedness nor a condition on the cohomology of $P$.

proof.text:
For any $R_T$-module $H$, construct the underived comparison
$$\beta_{T,n,H}:\operatorname{Res}_TH\otimes_{C_T}A_{n,T}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_T(H\otimes_{R_T}A_{n,T}),\qquad h\otimes\bar a\longmapsto h\otimes\bar a.$$
Both sides are the cokernel of multiplication by $\pi^n$ on the same underlying sheaf $H$: on the left use $A_{n,T}=C_T/(\pi^n)$, and on the right use $A_{n,T}=R_T/(\pi^n)$ from [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The two identifications send $h\otimes1$ to the class of $h$, so $\beta$ is invertible. This also proves the inverse formula, including balancing by arbitrary local $R_T$-sections, without assuming that those sections are constant. Applying it degreewise gives a natural chain isomorphism. On each tensor generator both orders of reduction from $n+1$ to $n$ send $h\otimes\bar a$ to $h\otimes(\bar a\bmod\pi^n)$, and $\beta$ sends the quotient augmentation $h\mapsto h\otimes1$ to the same augmentation. Thus all these compatibilities are strict.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat; quotient tensor universal property, explicitly computed

proof.text:
Use the ordinary balanced tensor comparison of [def-sfb-condensed-pullback-tensor-comparison] with $H=P^q$ and the coefficient module $A_{n,Y}$, and identify $g^*A_{n,Y}=A_{n,X}$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Degreewise this gives $\lambda_n:T_n\cong U_n$. The same balanced calculation over $C$ gives $g_C^*(Q\otimes_{C_Y}A_{n,Y})\cong(g_C^*Q)\otimes_{C_X}A_{n,X}$. Under inverse-coefficient transport its formula is the balanced map sending the inverse-image tensor $h\otimes\bar a$ to the tensor of the two inverse images; it commutes with differentials by naturality in $P^q$. Define
$$\theta_n=g_C^*(\beta_{Y,n,P}^{-1})\circ d_{P\otimes_{R_Y}A_{n,Y}}:\operatorname{Res}_XT_n\xrightarrow{\sim}V_n.$$
Here step 2 constructs $d$ for all complexes, so it applies even though the finite tensor need not be K-flat. The formulas for $\beta$ and $d$ show that $\theta_n$ also sends an inverse-image tensor $h\otimes\bar a$ to the same tensor. For either $\lambda$ or $\theta$, composing in either order with the transition sends this generator to $h\otimes(\bar a\bmod\pi^n)$. Composing with the augmentation sends $h$ to $h\otimes1$; on the source of $\theta$ this uses $d_P(h)=h$. These generator equations prove equality of sheaf maps, hence of chain maps. Thus $\lambda$ and $\theta$ are isomorphisms of strict towers, preserving their specified augmentations.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is the identity on underlying abelian sheaves [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Kernels and local lifts of sections through epimorphisms are therefore unchanged, so it is exact. Products of module sheaves exist and are computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Consequently the canonical map $\operatorname{Res}_X(\prod_nT_n)\to\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_XT_n$ is an isomorphism: over every site object it sends a tuple to that same tuple, and both $C_X$-actions are componentwise. It commutes with projections, differentials and $s$. Finite direct sums and their maps are unchanged as well. This fixes the product and cone identifications used for $E_P$.

source.place: Comparison with the Stacks Project: exactness and preservation of products under restriction

proof.text:
For $W$ put $B_W=\prod_nW_n$ and $F_W=1-s_W$. In the coordinate order fixed in the statement,
$$\mathsf R(W)^q=B_W^{q-1}\oplus B_W^q,\qquad D_W(y,x)=(-d_Wy-F_Wx,d_Wx).$$
Let $a=\prod_n\lambda_n$ and let $e=\prod_n\theta_n$, using step 6 for the source of $e$. Strict transition compatibility from step 5 gives $aF_T=F_Ua$ and $eF_{\operatorname{Res}T}=F_Ve$. Define $L_P(y,x)=(ay,ax)$ and $E_P(y,x)=(ey,ex)$. For example,
$$D_U(ay,ax)=(-a\,d_Ty-aF_Tx,a\,d_Tx)=L_P D_T(y,x).$$
The identical computation with $e$ proves the chain equation for $E_P$. Their inverses are diagonal products of the levelwise inverses and satisfy the same equations. Naturality in $P$ follows from the natural level maps and the componentwise product formulas. Thus these are precisely the asserted cochain isomorphisms, with no cone-map choice.

proof.text:
For a compatible augmentation $b:L\to W$, set $b^\Pi=(b_n)_n$. Compatibility says $F_Wb^\Pi=0$. Hence
$$D_W(0,b^\Pi z)=(0,b^\Pi d_Lz),$$
so the specified $\alpha_W(z)=(0,b^\Pi z)$ is a chain map with exactly the given cone signs. Step 5 gives $a b_T^\Pi=b_U^\Pi$ and $e\operatorname{Res}_X(b_T^\Pi)=b_V^\Pi d$. Evaluating the diagonal maps of step 7 now gives
$$L_P\alpha_T(z)=(0,b_U^\Pi z)=\alpha_U(z),\qquad E_P\operatorname{Res}_X(\alpha_T)(z)=(0,b_V^\Pi d(z))=\alpha_Vd(z).$$
These are equalities of actual chain maps, rather than equalities inferred only from their finite projections.

proof.text: It remains to identify these actual cone maps with the total derived strict-tower comparisons. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], products are exact for each coefficient sheaf here. Thus [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus] applies: its reordered cone is exactly $\mathsf R(W)$ with coordinates $(x,y)$, and its action on strict maps is the diagonal product map of step 7. For a K-injective tower resolution $W\to I$, as used in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], this gives a quasi-isomorphism $\mathsf R(W)\to\mathsf R(I)$. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-roos-complex] the natural map $\varprojlim I_n\to\mathsf R(I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, explicitly $z\mapsto(0,(z_n)_n)$. The remaining hypothesis of the K-injective Roos lemma holds: the module category on a small pro-étale skeleton is Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The strict tower resolution is supplied by the ringed strict-tower theorem. The resulting zigzag identifies $Q\mathsf R(W)$ with the total right derived inverse limit. For an augmented tower, both composites from $L$ to $\mathsf R(I)$ are $(0,(L\to W_n\to I_n)_n)$, so this zigzag identifies the augmentation with the strict-derived-tower unit. Where the unit is defined as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], through a resolution $\Delta L\to I'$ and $R\lim$ of $\Delta L\to W$, choose a lift $I'\to I$; by K-injectivity of $I$ its composite with $\Delta L\to I'$ is homotopic to $\Delta L\to W\to I$, and the diagonal product of that homotopy is a homotopy on $\mathsf R(I)$, so both descriptions give the same map in the derived category. It is natural in strict maps; hence the localizations of $L_P,E_P$ are the claimed canonical comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms of Roos triangles.

proof.text: By step 3, $P$, $g^*P$, $Q$ and $g_C^*Q$ are valid flat-term K-flat representatives for their respective derived tensor calculations [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus $U$ computes the finite derived reductions of $g^*[P]$, and $V$ computes those of $g_C^*[Q]$ (constant-coefficient inverse image commutes with reduction by the same balanced calculation of step 5). The quotient-tower units are the derived-completion units by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], including for inputs which are not complete. In the notation of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], use the identification of step 1 [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] of its $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ with $R_T$. Its structure map $c_g$ is then $a_R$ of step 2: naturality of $g^{-1}p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ at $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_E/\pi^n$ [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] gives the $n$-th projection of $a_R$ as the constant-sheaf comparison $g^{-1}(A_n)_Y\cong(A_n)_X$, which, like the $n$-th component of $c_g$, sends each constant section to itself; maps into the limit agree when their projections do. So module pullback along $c_g$ is the item's $g^*$. Applying derived pullback to the augmented strict reduction tower gives the tower represented here by $T$: inverse image on $R$-modules is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], so it computes this operation on any representative of the tower. Step 9 identifies its chosen total derived inverse limit and unit with $Q\mathsf R(T)$ and $Q\alpha_T$. Therefore step 8 proves both required normalized derived identities. On derived-complete input the constant formula is precisely Stacks completed pullback (099N(2),(5)); on arbitrary input it is the same ordinary pullback followed by completion and its unit. This argument never identifies the two ambient coefficient categories, or asserts that an arbitrary $[P]$ is complete.
